title: 4×4 Box Breathing
clinicalIntent: Structured breathing to support nervous system regulation without strain. Helps shift from sympathetic activation toward parasympathetic calm.
contraindications: Severe COPD or breathing difficulty without clinician guidance

steps.label: Inhale
steps.description: Inhale gently through the nose for a count of 4.

steps.label: Hold
steps.description: Hold the breath softly for a count of 4. No straining—if uncomfortable, shorten or skip.

steps.label: Exhale
steps.description: Exhale slowly through the mouth for a count of 4.

steps.label: Rest
steps.description: Pause and rest for a count of 4 before the next breath cycle.

aftercare: Notice how your body feels. If you feel lightheaded, return to normal breathing and rest.
whenToEscalate: If you experience chest pain, severe dizziness, or breathing difficulty, stop and seek medical attention. In crisis, call 988 (U.S.) or local emergency services.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 Senses Grounding
clinicalIntent: Sensory reconnection to the present moment when internal experience feels too loud or overwhelming. Anchors attention in the here-and-now.
contraindications: None for general use. Proceed gently; stop any step that increases distress.

steps.label: 5 things you see
steps.description: Gently look around and name 5 things you can see, out loud or silently.

steps.label: 4 things you feel
steps.description: Notice 4 things you can feel through touch: feet on floor, clothing, chair, air on skin.

steps.label: 3 things you hear
steps.description: Name 3 sounds you can hear right now, even faint ones.

steps.label: 2 things you smell
steps.description: Notice 2 things you can smell, or remember a calming smell.

steps.label: 1 thing you taste
steps.description: Notice 1 thing about the taste in your mouth, or imagine a comforting taste.

aftercare: Take a few natural breaths. You can repeat this sequence if needed.
whenToEscalate: If you feel increasingly unsafe or disconnected, stop and reach out to a trusted person or crisis line. Call 988 (U.S.) if you are in danger or considering self-harm.

title: Panic Anchoring: Feet and Breath
clinicalIntent: Short reset to help the body remember it has ground and breath when panic or fear spikes. Minimal cognitive load, maximum physical anchoring.
contraindications: None. Safe to use during acute distress. Stop if any step worsens symptoms.

steps.label: Find your feet
steps.description: Notice your feet on the floor or any surface. Press them down gently and feel the contact.

steps.label: Long exhale
steps.description: Take a slow breath in, then a longer, softer exhale—as if gently fogging a mirror.

steps.label: Name safety cues
steps.description: Look for 2 or 3 signs that you are physically safe right now: a closed door, trusted objects, your own breathing.

aftercare: Stay with your breath. Repeat the exhale step as often as needed. No pressure to fix anything quickly.
whenToEscalate: If panic does not ease or you feel in danger, call 988 (U.S.) or local emergency services. You deserve support.

title: Anchoring Protocol
clinicalIntent: For panic states—immediate physical and breath-based anchoring. Simple, repetitive, body-focused. Trauma-informed.
contraindications: None. Designed for acute use. Proceed at your own pace.

steps.label: Hand on chest
steps.description: Place your hand over your chest. Feel the warmth and gentle pressure.

steps.label: Slow exhale
steps.description: Exhale slowly, making the exhale longer than the inhale. Repeat 3–4 times.

steps.label: Count breaths
steps.description: Count your breaths: 1 on inhale, 2 on exhale. Give your mind something simple to focus on.

aftercare: Stay with your hand on your chest as long as it feels supportive.
whenToEscalate: If distress increases or you feel unsafe, stop and call 988 (U.S.) or local emergency services.

title: Standard Ritual Sequence
clinicalIntent: Gentle nervous system protocol: pause, ground, orient, release. For general regulation and daily reset.
contraindications: None. Proceed gently; pause any step that feels too much.

steps.label: Pause and arrive
steps.description: Take a moment to pause and arrive in this space. No rush.

steps.label: Breathe slowly
steps.description: Breathe slowly and naturally, letting your body settle.

steps.label: Soft body scan
steps.description: Gently scan your body from head to toe, noticing sensations without judgment.

steps.label: Release tension
steps.description: Release any tension you notice, without forcing. Allow, don't push.

aftercare: Notice how you feel. You can repeat the sequence if helpful.
whenToEscalate: If you experience increased distress or dissociation, stop and reach out for support. Call 988 (U.S.) if in crisis.

title: Hand-on-Heart Shame Soften
clinicalIntent: Gentle self-contact and self-talk protocol for when shame feels heavy or the mind is attacking itself. Validates experience without dismissing.
contraindications: If touch feels unsafe, use a soft object or imagine the gesture. Proceed only as far as feels okay.

steps.label: Hand placement
steps.description: Place a hand over your chest or another area that feels safe to touch.

steps.label: Anchor breath
steps.description: Take 3 slow, natural breaths, noticing your hand rise and fall.

steps.label: Gentle statement
steps.description: Quietly repeat a kind phrase: 'It makes sense that I feel this way,' or 'I am allowed to be human in this moment.'

steps.label: Stay with warmth
steps.description: Stay with the feeling of your hand resting there. Imagine warmth or soft light if that helps.

aftercare: Language must never blame. All phrases should validate experience, not dismiss it.
whenToEscalate: If shame intensifies or you feel increasingly isolated, reach out to a trusted person or professional. Call 988 (U.S.) if you are in danger or considering self-harm.

title: Grief Wave Seat
clinicalIntent: Practice for sitting with a wave of grief in a way that honors it without drowning in it. Accompaniment, not exposure.
contraindications: If grief feels overwhelming or destabilizing, pause and seek support. This is not exposure therapy.

steps.label: Choose a position
steps.description: Sit or lie in a position that feels as safe as possible for a few minutes.

steps.label: Name the wave
steps.description: Quietly name the wave: 'A wave of grief is here,' or whatever language feels right.

steps.label: Stay close to breath
steps.description: Let your breath move naturally, as if breathing alongside the grief instead of against it.

steps.label: Set a gentle limit
steps.description: Tell yourself: 'For these next few minutes I will just stay with this wave. It does not have to be resolved.'

aftercare: Permission to stop at any time. This is accompaniment, not endurance. Be gentle with yourself.
whenToEscalate: If grief becomes overwhelming or you feel unable to cope, stop and reach out for support. Call 988 (U.S.) if you are in danger or considering self-harm.

title: Orienting Protocol
clinicalIntent: For freeze states—helps reconnect with the present moment and environment. Trauma-informed: gentle, non-overwhelming, sensory-based.
contraindications: If orienting increases distress, stop and try a simpler anchor (e.g., feet on floor, one breath).

steps.label: Look around safely
steps.description: Look around your environment, noticing what feels safe. No pressure to name everything.

steps.label: Name 5 objects
steps.description: Name 5 objects you can see. They can be simple: a wall, a window, a chair.

steps.label: Feel feet on ground
steps.description: Feel your feet on the ground. Notice the support beneath you. Press down gently if that helps.

aftercare: You can repeat the feet-on-ground step as often as needed.
whenToEscalate: If you feel increasingly disconnected or unsafe, stop and reach out to a trusted person. Call 988 (U.S.) if in crisis.
